p060.lead: The sudden rise of the reptiles, the reign and fall of the dinosaurs, the coming of flowers and birds, and the birth of mountains: the hundred-million-year story of the Mesozoic.

p060.foot.text: Presented by a Life Carrier of Nebadon assigned to Satania and now functioning on Urantia

p060.s0.h: Introduction — The End of the Sea-Only Age
p060.s0.b0: Paper 60 follows the marine-life era with the early land-life era, the hundred million years that geologists call the Mesozoic. Rising land, cooling crust and oceans, shrinking seas, and a great increase of land in the northern latitudes worked together to change the climate in every region far from the equator. In this way the age when life existed only in the sea came to an end.

p060.s0.b1.q: The era of exclusive marine life has ended.

p060.s0.b2: The starting point was meager. Very few types had outlived the biologic tribulation at the close of the preceding era; the frogs survived in greatly reduced numbers, and even the spore-bearing plants were nearly extinct. From that thin beginning, the paper traces in three periods how dinosaurs overran the land, then vanished, and how flowers and birds appeared.

p060.s1.h: I. The Early Reptilian Age — Reptiles Appear Suddenly
p060.s1.b0: The gypsum and red layers in the deposits of this period show that the climate of America and Europe was arid. Fossils are scarce, but many sandstone footprints of land reptiles remain, and the life of land animals continued unbroken only in certain parts of Africa. The Palisades of the Hudson River, the dolomite limestone of the southern Alps, and Carrara marble are traces of this time.
p060.s1.b1: When the era opened 150 million years ago, the eastern and central parts of North America, most of Europe, and all of Asia stood well above water. North America was geographically isolated for the first time, though the Bering Strait land bridge soon reappeared to join it to Asia. Great troughs such as the eastern-Connecticut fault formed and were later filled with erosion deposits, and the petrified forests of many regions belong to this epoch. Life did not fare well, but it did better than at the harsh close of the previous era.
p060.s1.b2: Then, 140 million years ago, with only the hint of two prereptilian ancestors that had developed in Africa, the reptiles appeared suddenly in full-fledged form. They soon gave rise to crocodiles, scaled reptiles, sea serpents, and flying reptiles, and the dinosaurs became the monarchs of the age. The early dinosaurs were small and carnivorous, and they walked kangaroolike on their hind legs.

p060.s1.b3.q: They were egg layers and are distinguished from all animals by their small brains, having brains weighing less than one pound to control bodies later weighing as much as forty tons.

p060.s1.b4: Several million years later the first mammals appeared, but they were nonplacental and soon failed; none survived. The author records this plainly as an experiment that did not succeed. In the seas, hosts of beautiful ammonites flourished, and on the Californian coast alone over a thousand species of them developed.

p060.s1.b5.q: This was an experimental effort to improve mammalian types, but it did not succeed on Urantia.

p060.s2.h: II. The Later Reptilian Age — The Dead End of Sheer Size
p060.s2.b0: The great event of the Jurassic, which began 120 million years ago, was the evolution and decline of the dinosaurs. They came in every size, from species less than two feet long to huge plant-eaters seventy-five feet long. But the larger they grew, the less active and strong they became; they needed enormous amounts of food, and the land was so overrun with them that in the end they starved.

p060.s2.b1.q: they literally starved to death and became extinct—they lacked the intelligence to cope with the situation.

p060.s2.b2: The Jurassic was also a fresh-water age of many inland lakes, as the rich fresh-water fossils of the Morrison beds of Colorado, Montana, and Wyoming show. The sea’s invasion was greatest in Europe, where the beautiful lithographic stone of southern Germany was laid down. The returning seas improved the weather: corals spread to European waters, ammonites dominated the invertebrate life of the oceans, and a sturgeon type of fish and the modern crustaceans appeared.

p060.s2.b3.q: fossils, such as the most delicate wings of olden insects, are preserved as of but yesterday.

p060.s2.b4: This section also shows that evolution does not always move forward. Two species of dinosaurs, crowded off the land, took to the water and became sea serpents; two other types were driven into the air and became pterosaurs. Neither line lasted, for their brains were far too small for their bodies.

p060.s2.b6.q: While some new species are progressing, certain strains remain stationary and others gravitate backward, reverting to a former state.

p060.s2.b7: By one hundred million years ago the reptilian age was drawing to a close. At this point the author declares that the direction of evolution is changing. This short sentence is the key to the whole of Paper 60.

p060.s2.b8.q: Henceforth, evolution will follow the growth of brains, not physical bulk, and the development of brains will characterize each succeeding epoch of animal evolution and planetary progress.

p060.s3.h: III. The Cretaceous Stage — The Flowering-Plant Period — The Age of Birds
p060.s3.b0: The Cretaceous takes its name from the chalk-making foraminifers that dominated the seas. In this period the drifting continents met the deep floor of the Pacific, and the great north-south range from Alaska to Cape Horn began to rise, opening the modern mountain-building stage of geologic history. When the westward drift halted 80 million years ago, its momentum crumpled up the Pacific shore line, producing the circumpacific uplift more than twenty-five thousand miles long—the greatest surface distortion since life appeared.
p060.s3.b1: The strata of this period left other gifts as well. Layers of pure clay, now used for making earthenware, were laid down along the Atlantic coast, together with chalk, greensand marl, lignite, and oil-bearing deposits. Porous layers permeated with chalk take in water at their outcrops and carry it downward, supplying water to many of today’s arid regions. When the Bering Strait closed 85 million years ago, the marine life of the Atlantic-Gulf waters and the Pacific became uniform.
p060.s3.b2: Continental drift ended 75 million years ago. The Pacific coast ranges from Alaska to Cape Horn were complete, though as yet with few peaks. The backthrust of the halted drift kept raising the western plains of North America, and when the Rocky Mountain region reached its maximum elevation 70 million years ago, Cambrian rocks in British Columbia were thrust fifteen miles out over Cretaceous layers. Places where older strata lie on top of younger ones call for care when reading the earth’s history.
p060.s3.b3: Ninety million years ago the angiosperms appeared suddenly, along with fig trees, magnolias, and tulip trees, and soon overran the continents. Many of today’s trees—beech, oak, maple, and others—appeared for the first time, and fruits, grasses, and cereals became abundant. The author compares the significance of these seed-bearing plants to the appearance of man.

p060.s3.b4.q: they were second in evolutionary importance only to the appearance of man himself.

p060.s3.b5: Two attempts to produce flying creatures had failed. The wading and swimming prebirds and the flying dinosaurs both died out, having too little brain for the size of their bodies. Then, 55 million years ago, a small pigeonlike true bird suddenly appeared, springing directly from the reptilian group. It became the ancestor of all bird life.
p060.s3.b6: The climate was still warm and uniform; even the arctic regions enjoyed weather like that of central and southern North America today. Sixty million years ago the dinosaurs were still monarchs of the land, but now the smaller, agile carnivorous types took the lead, and with the appearance of grasses, new plant-eating dinosaurs with two horns and a shoulder flange multiplied rapidly. Land turtles twenty feet across, the modern crocodile, and true snakes also appeared.

p060.s3.b8.q: And so this becomes known as the age of birds as well as the declining age of reptiles.

p060.s4.h: IV. The End of the Chalk Period — Mountains Born and the Next Stage Set
p060.s4.b0: The close of the Cretaceous ended the great sea invasions of the continents. North America had undergone just twenty-four great inundations, with land and sea alternating in dominance in million-year cycles. These rhythmic crustal movements will continue, but with diminishing frequency and extent.
p060.s4.b1: The chief factor determining where a mountain range forms is not continental pressure but a pre-existing lowland or trough filled with lighter deposits. When the crust is put under pressure, these lighter areas are the first to crumple and rise. Today’s Rocky Mountains are not the original elevation; that land was leveled by erosion and then raised again, and Pikes Peak and Longs Peak span two or more generations of mountain lives.

p060.s4.b3: At the end of this period the ammonites declined rapidly, and the fern forests gave way to pines and other modern trees, including the giant redwoods. There were still no placental mammals, but the stage was fully set for the ancestors of the future mammals to appear.

p060.s4.b4.q: the biologic stage is fully set for the appearance, in a subsequent age, of the early ancestors of the future mammalian types.

p060.s5.b0: The central lesson of Paper 60 is that intelligence matters more than size. Dinosaurs that ruled forty-ton bodies with brains of less than a pound flourished until they covered the land, yet they vanished because they lacked the intelligence to meet their situation. From then on, evolution follows the growth of brains rather than bulk. The paper also does not hide failed experiments—the first mammals and two attempts at flying creatures—and it shows that the true birds and the flowering plants came after them.

p060.s5.b2: Paper 61 turns to the mammalian era that unfolds on this stage. From the appearance of the placental mammals to the ice age and the coming of man, we follow where an evolution guided by the growth of brains finally leads.
p061.lead: From the first placental mammals through the age of elephants and horses, six ice invasions, and the first human beings: the fifty-million-year record of the Cenozoic.

p061.s0.h: Introduction — From Animal Paradise to the Cradle of Man
p061.s0.b0: Paper 61 is the last of the papers that chronicle Urantia’s geologic history. The era of mammals runs from the origin of the placental mammals to the end of the ice age, a span of a little less than fifty million years. Its landscape was one of rolling hills, broad valleys, wide rivers, and great forests, and the trees were full of birds.

p061.s0.b1.q: The trees swarmed with birds, and the whole world was an animal paradise, notwithstanding the incessant struggle of the evolving animal species for supremacy.

p061.s0.b2: The deposits of the five periods of these fifty million years hold the fossil records of one mammalian dynasty after another, leading right up to the actual appearance of man. So this paper is at once a history of animals and the story of how the stage was prepared for human beings.

p061.s1.h: I. The Age of Early Mammals — The Placental Mammals Appear
p061.s1.b0: Fifty million years ago the placental mammals suddenly appeared in North America. Nonplacental mammals had existed before, but this new type sprang directly from a reptilian ancestor whose descendants had lived on through the decline of the dinosaurs. The author calls this the most important evolutionary development up to that time.

p061.s1.b1.q: The father of the placental mammals was a small, highly active, carnivorous, springing type of dinosaur.

p061.s1.b2: In these primitive mammals the basic mammalian instincts began to show themselves. The paper lists five reasons why mammals have an immense survival advantage over all other animals. The second of them—that they feed, train, and protect their young with affectionate regard—shows that love and care are themselves a power for survival.

p061.s1.b4: By 45 million years ago small horses, fleet-footed rhinoceroses, tapirs, primitive pigs, squirrels, lemurs, opossums, and monkeylike animals lived in the forests. There was also a large ostrichlike bird ten feet tall, an ancestor of the later highly intelligent passenger birds that once carried human beings through the air. The mammals of this time were all covered with hair and had large brains for their size, but no modern forms yet existed.
p061.s1.b5: Later in this epoch most of Europe was submerged, with the highlands of the Alps and the Pyrenees standing up as islands. The foraminiferal limestone laid down in European waters at that time now stands 16,000 feet high in the Himalayas and 20,000 feet in Tibet. North America was joined by land to every continent except Australia, and the world was overrun by primitive mammals.
p061.s2.h: II. The Age of Advanced Mammals — Brains Replace Armor
p061.s2.b0: Thirty-five million years ago marks the beginning of placental-mammal dominion over the world. From carnivorous ancestors there soon branched herbivorous and then omnivorous families, and the angiosperms were their principal food. Before the period ended, over a hundred species of primitive mammals were extinct, and even the large mammals with small brains soon perished.

p061.s2.b1.q: Brains and agility had replaced armor and size in the progress of animal survival.

p061.s2.b2: In this period the ancestors of dogs, cats, coons, and weasels appeared, along with gnawing rodents such as beavers, squirrels, and rabbits. From 30 million years ago the grazing, hoofed animals of the plains evolved, in contrast to the earlier mammals of the hills. Camels and llamas originated in North America and later migrated, the camels to Europe and the llamas to South America. And in western North America the early ancestors of the ancient lemurs first appeared, establishing the line from which the true lemurs would later spring.
p061.s2.b3: Meanwhile, just as the land serpents of an earlier age had gone to sea, a whole tribe of placental mammals forsook the land for the oceans, giving rise to whales, dolphins, seals, and sea lions. By the close of the Oligocene, which lasted ten million years, life on earth looked very much as it does today.
p061.s3.h: III. Age of the Elephant and the Horse — A Brain Equal to the Body
p061.s3.b0: Twenty million years ago was truly the golden age of mammals. The Bering Strait land bridge rose, mastodons and many members of the cat family crossed from Asia to North America, and the first deer appeared. For once the world was dominated by a huge animal with a brain large enough for its body: the elephant.

p061.s3.b1.q: In intelligence and adaptation the elephant is approached only by the horse and is surpassed only by man himself.

p061.s3.b2: The author draws an interesting comparison between the elephant and the horse. It shows that intelligence is tied not only to the size of the brain but also to the ability to govern one’s emotions.

p061.s3.b4: This section contains a rare word addressed directly to the reader. As Urantia enters the so-called “horseless age,” we are asked to pause and consider what this animal meant to our ancestors. Men used horses first for food, then for travel, and later in agriculture and war, and the horse played an important part in the growth of civilization.

p061.s3.b5.q: The horse has long served mankind and has played an important part in the development of human civilization.

p061.s3.b6: During this period the true types of the primitive monkey and the gorilla evolved in central Asia. But the author states clearly that neither of these species belongs to the line that would later become the ancestors of the human race.
p061.s4.h: IV. The Last Great Mammalian Migration — The Hemispheres Divide
p061.s4.b0: Preglacial land elevation raised mountain ranges and changed the courses of rivers, and Shasta, Hood, and Rainier began their mountain careers. For a short time all the land of the world except Australia was joined once more, and the last great world-wide animal migration took place. Sloths, armadillos, and bears entered North America, while North American camels went to China.
p061.s4.b1: By 5 million years ago the horse had evolved into its present form and spread from North America to all the world, yet it died out on its continent of origin long before the red man arrived. As the climate cooled, the northern land bridges sank and the link between Africa and South America was cut. From then on the Eastern and Western Hemispheres each developed life of their own. When this period closed, the ancestor of man had still not appeared.

p061.s4.b2.q: From this time forward distinct types of life began to develop in the Eastern and Western Hemispheres.

p061.s5.h: V. The Early Ice Age — How Snow Became Ice
p061.s5.b0: The ice age was not caused by cold alone. Northeastern North America and northern Europe rose high, ocean currents and seasonal winds shifted, and saturated air dropped almost constant snow over the northern highlands. The snow piled up to a depth of 20,000 feet and turned into solid but creeping ice. Half of the glacial ice lay in North America, a quarter in Eurasia, and the rest chiefly in Antarctica.
p061.s5.b1: The northern regions experienced six distinct ice invasions, each with scores of advances and retreats. Two million years ago the first glacier began moving south, taking nearly a million years to advance and withdraw. Yet away from the ice, life changed little, and between the invasions the climate was about as mild as today, perhaps a little warmer.
p061.s6.h: VI. Primitive Man in the Ice Age — Born in a Hard Environment
p061.s6.b0: The great event of the glacial period was the evolution of primitive man. On land just west of India, now under water, the dawn mammals suddenly appeared among the offspring of Asiatic migrants of the older North American lemur types. Three great mutations followed.

p061.s6.b2: At the same time a retrograde development within the mid-mammal stock gave rise to the simian ancestry. From that day on the human branch went forward, while the simian tribes stood still or slipped back. One million years ago Urantia was registered as an inhabited world.

p061.s6.b3.q: 1,000,000 years ago Urantia was registered as an inhabited world.

p061.s6.b4.q: your early ancestors were born and bred in a stimulating, invigorating, and difficult environment.

p061.s6.b5: The first human beings were born about the time the third glacier began to advance. The Eskimos, the sole survivors of these aborigines, still prefer frigid northern climes. Man did not reach the Western Hemisphere until near the end of the ice age, but during the interglacial epochs he passed west around the Mediterranean and soon spread over Europe.
p061.s7.h: VII. The Continuing Ice Age — Landscapes Carved by Ice and Milestones of Mankind
p061.s7.b0: No other earthly activity leaves such characteristic marks as ice. Potholes, lakes, displaced stones, drumlins, and moraines are all the work of glaciers. As the sixth glacier retreated it produced North America’s Great Lakes, and it is thirty-seven thousand years since they began to empty out over the present Niagara route.
p061.s7.b1: Woven through this chronicle of ice are the decisive events of human history. Geologic time and spiritual history are set side by side on a single timeline.

p061.s7.b3: The sixth glacier, beginning 250,000 years ago, was the largest invasion of all, with three ice sheets merging into one. The harsh glacial period wiped out many species and radically changed others. Arctic plants and animals that fled up the mountains to escape the ice were stranded there when it withdrew, and they are still found high in the Alps and the Appalachians. As long as the polar regions remain covered with ice, we are told, another glacial age is hardly possible.

p061.s7.b4.q: Many were sorely sifted by the to-and-fro migration which was made necessary by the advancing and retreating ice.

p061.s8.b0: The planetary chronicle that began in Paper 57 reaches the birth of man in this paper. Over fifty million years brains and agility replaced armor and size, and the animals that cared for their young with affection inherited the world. And the first human beings were born not in a comfortable paradise but in a hard and stimulating environment with glaciers on the advance. That difficulty can be a condition for growth is the long-standing comfort this paper offers us.

p062.lead: From small mammals of the lemur type to Andon and Fonta: the story of how, after three sudden leaps, a mind with will was born.

p062.s0.h: Introduction — Where Did Man Come From?
p062.s0.b0: In Paper 62 a Life Carrier resident on Urantia introduces, one after another, the immediate animal ancestors of mankind. About one million years ago, three successive and sudden mutations from early stock of the lemur type of placental mammal produced human beings. The paper follows these three stages under the names dawn mammals, mid-mammals, and Primates.
p062.s0.b1: The paper also sets out the line of descent. The dominant factors came from the western, or later American, life group, reinforced by contributions from the central life implantation that evolved in Africa; the eastern life group contributed little or nothing to the actual production of the human species. The paper is a biological chronicle, but it is also the record of the moment when mind and will first awoke.
p062.s1.h: I. The Early Lemur Types — A Long Migration to a Sheltered Peninsula
p062.s1.b0: The early lemurs in mankind’s ancestry were not directly related to the gibbons and apes then living in Eurasia and northern Africa. Nor were they descended from the modern lemur; the ancestor the two shared has long been extinct. Several million years ago North American lemurs crossed the Bering land bridge westward and slowly worked their way southwest along the Asiatic coast.
p062.s1.b1: They came at last to a salubrious region west of India, between the then expanded Mediterranean and the rising mountains of the Indian peninsula. Later the coast sank, and this Mesopotamian or Persian peninsula became isolated, reachable only from the north—and that route was often cut off by glaciers. In this sheltered corner two great groups branched apart: the simian tribes of modern times and the human species.
p062.s2.h: II. The Dawn Mammals — The Beginnings of Fear and Tribal Spirit
p062.s2.b0: A little more than one million years ago the Mesopotamian dawn mammals suddenly appeared. They were active little flesh eaters almost three feet tall, able to stand erect with ease, and they had a primitive opposable thumb. For their size they had the largest brains of any animal yet to exist, and they showed curiosity, elation at success, tenderness in the family, and a sense of self-abasement bordering on shame.
p062.s2.b1: They reached full growth at three or four years of age and had a potential life span of about twenty years. They were touchingly loyal to their mates and fought fiercely to defend their kindred. Even in so short a life, the outline of the emotions and instincts that would later mark man was already being drawn.
p062.s2.b2: Because they were small and keenly aware of the dangers of the forest, these creatures developed an extraordinary fear, which led them to wise precautions such as building shelters in the high treetops. Here the Life Carrier points to one root of the human temperament.

p062.s2.b3.q: The beginning of the fear tendencies of mankind more specifically dates from these days.

p062.s2.b4: They were highly gregarious yet quick to fight, and through selective survival, as superior groups warred on inferior neighbors, the species steadily improved. Just seventy generations after their origin from the highest lemur ancestor, the ancestors of the next stage suddenly appeared.
p062.s3.h: III. The Mid-Mammals — Where Man and Ape Parted Ways
p062.s3.b0: In the treetop home of a superior pair of dawn mammals, twins were born. This brother and sister grew to a little over four feet tall, walked upright, and had almost perfectly opposable thumbs. From early on they were recognized as heads of the tribe, and they instituted a primitive form of social organization and a crude division of labor. Their twenty-one children formed the nucleus of the mid-mammals.
p062.s3.b1: The mid-mammals could show disgust, hid food for later use, and had a hoarding instinct for collecting stones. They were the first mammals to provide for safety in both treetop and underground shelters. But as their numbers grew, competition for food and mates led to internecine battles that nearly destroyed the species, until only one group of fewer than a hundred was left.

p062.s3.b2.q: You can hardly realize by what narrow margins your prehuman ancestors missed extinction from time to time.

p062.s3.b3: The closest call was a lightning bolt. It struck the tree where the future parents of the Primates twins were sleeping and killed three of their seven children. The surviving couple led the more progressive group about two miles away, and there the first Primates twins were born. At the same time an inferior pair in the tribe also had twins, and these became the founders of the modern simian tribes.

p062.s3.b5: So the paper draws a clear line in describing the relation between man and the apes. They came from the same tribe and species, but not from the same parents; they are linked only through their common origin in the mid-mammals.

p062.s3.b6.q: Modern man and the simians did spring from the same tribe and species but not from the same parents.

p062.s3.b7: In this section chance and choice overlap. Even within one tribe, what was chosen made a great difference in where the descendants would go.

The Primates had fully developed human hands and feet, yet they did not have minds that could really be called human. After almost nine hundred generations, about twenty-one thousand years from the origin of the dawn mammals, the Primates gave birth to the first two true human beings.

p063.s1.h: I–II. Andon and Fonta; The Flight of the Twins — The First to Kindle Fire
p063.s1.b0: In many respects Andon and Fonta were the most remarkable pair of human beings ever to live on earth. They were superior to many of their immediate descendants and radically different from all their ancestors. While still living with his parents, Andon bound a sharp flint to the end of a club with animal tendons, and on at least a dozen occasions this weapon saved his life and his sister’s. Their vague sense of being more than mere animals came from their possession of personality and was heightened by the indwelling Thought Adjusters.
p063.s1.b1: The decision to leave was not easy. They feared displeasing their father and family, and they knew that their already jealous tribesmen might kill them. But one night, after a violent storm had awakened them, holding each other in a fearful and fond embrace, they finally made up their minds to go.

p063.s1.b3: The discovery of fire was the fruit of partnership: the idea was Andon’s, but it was Fonta who unlocked the secret. Their Primates ancestors had often kept alive fires kindled by lightning, but never before had any creature on earth possessed a way of starting fire at will.

p063.s1.b4.q: This was one of the most joyous moments in their short but eventful lives.

p063.s1.b5: All night they sat watching the fire, dimly realizing that this discovery would let them defy the climate and so be forever independent of their animal relatives in the south. A single discovery had changed the whole setting of their lives.
p063.s2.h: III. Andon’s Family — The Instinct to Care and the Spirit of the Clan
p063.s2.b0: Almost two years after their flight their first child, Sontad, was born. He was the first creature on Urantia to be wrapped in protective coverings at birth, and from this time appeared the instinct to care for increasingly helpless infants. The Life Carrier sees in this a sign that mind of the intellectual order was developing.
p063.s2.b2: Andon and Fonta had nineteen children and lived to see almost fifty grandchildren and six great-grandchildren. The family lived in rock shelters, some joined by hallways dug out of the soft limestone, and with a marked clannish spirit they hunted together and stayed close to home. This sense of intimate kinship, we are told, came from the enhanced ministry of the adjutant spirits. The two died together at forty-two, killed by a rock that fell during an earthquake.
p063.s2.b3: Though his foot was seriously injured, Sontad at once took up leadership of the clan and rolled up stones to entomb the dead. The paper cautions, however, against reading too much into this burial: their ideas of survival after death were vague and largely drawn from their dream life. The family held together until the twentieth generation, when food competition and social friction began to scatter it.
p063.s3.h: IV. The Andonic Clans — Foreshadowings of Nobility and Seeds of Division
p063.s3.b0: In describing primitive man, this section shows both what was already present and what was still missing. The men fought heroically for their mates and children, and the women were devoted to their young, but their loyalty stopped at the immediate clan. There was also a touching affection for comrades and a real, if crude, idea of friendship.

p063.s3.b2: These early humans were less sensitive to pain and unpleasant situations than many later mortals, and childbirth was not painful for Fonta and her immediate descendants. The clan kept an unbroken line of leadership through Sontad’s descendants until the twenty-seventh generation; when no male heir appeared, two rivals began to fight for supremacy. Even this early, a gap in leadership became a door to division.
p063.s3.b3: The paper describes their appearance simply. The Andonites had black eyes and a swarthy complexion, something between yellow and red, and melanin was the original Andonic skin pigment. They were the first creatures to use animal skins for protection against cold. They added new words almost daily and built a well-developed language, which remained the tongue of Urantia until the colored races appeared.
p063.s3.b4: But as their numbers grew, hunting and revenge came to occupy their minds, and clan warfare forever destroyed some of the ablest strains. The Life Carriers, knowing this tendency, provide for the eventual separation of evolving humans into several distinct races.

p063.s3.b5.q: Man is the descendant of fighting animals

p063.s4.h: V. Dispersion of the Andonites — North and West
p063.s4.b0: The early Andon races did not go deep into Asia or into Africa; following the lay of the land, they went north until the third glacier stopped them. Before the ice sheet reached France and the British Isles, they had spread west across Europe and founded more than a thousand settlements along the great rivers flowing to the then warm North Sea. That is why so much evidence of them is found along the Somme, a river whose course the glaciers did not change.
p063.s4.b1: They lived under overhanging cliffs along the rivers and in hillside grottoes where they could enjoy their fires, and they built dome-shaped stone huts, closing the entrance at night by rolling a stone placed inside for that purpose. As Andon had invented the stone ax, his descendants discovered the throwing stick and the harpoon, and they traveled far in search of flint.

p063.s4.b2.q: At last a tool-creating mind was functioning in conjunction with an implement-using hand

p063.s4.b3: The section ends on a sober contrast. In many ways the Andon tribes showed an intelligence that their retrogressing descendants did not reach again in half a million years; those descendants had to rediscover how to kindle fire again and again. The passage quietly shows that what one generation gains is not automatically inherited by the next.
p063.s5.h: VI. Onagar — The First Truth Teacher
p063.s5.b0: As the dispersion spread, the cultural and spiritual state of the clans declined for nearly ten thousand years. Then Onagar became their leader, brought peace among the tribes, and for the first time led them all in worship of the “⟦Q 63:6.1⟧Breath Giver to men and animals.⟦/Q⟧” Until then primitive religion had drifted with fear and hunger.

p063.s5.b2: The explanation of the origin of sacrifice is especially worth noting. The Andonites refrained from eating the flesh of the animal their tribe venerated, and to impress the young they held a ceremony around its body. This primitive rite grew into the more elaborate sacrifices of later times, and the text says the idea was carried on by Moses in the Hebrew ritual and preserved in principle by Paul in the doctrine of atonement.

p063.s5.b3.q: And this is the origin of sacrifices as a part of worship.

p063.s5.b4: How central food was to their lives can be seen in the prayer Onagar taught. Daily food, deliverance from the enemies of ice and forest, and hope for the life beyond are all contained in one short prayer.

p063.s5.b5.q: “O Breath of Life, give us this day our daily food, deliver us from the curse of the ice, save us from our forest enemies, and with mercy receive us into the Great Beyond.”

p063.s5.b6: Onagar kept his headquarters at Oban, near the present Caspian Sea, and sent teachers out to the remote settlements. These emissaries were the world’s first missionaries, and also the first to use fire regularly in preparing food. Born 983,323 years ago, he lived to sixty-nine and established a tribal government whose like was not attained for many millenniums. It was in his day that Thought Adjusters and guardian seraphim came to Urantia in great numbers.

p063.s5.b7.q: This was, indeed, the golden age of primitive man.

p063.s6.h: VII. The Survival of Andon and Fonta — Service on the Mansion Worlds
p063.s6.b0: The two founders of the human race were recognized at the adjudication that came with the arrival of the Planetary Prince, and they passed through the mansion worlds to citizenship on Jerusem. They grieved over the Caligastia betrayal and the Adamic failure, but rejoiced exceedingly when they learned that Michael had chosen their world for his final bestowal. On Jerusem, Andon and Fonta, Sontad, and several of their children fused with their Thought Adjusters, though most of their immediate descendants achieved Spirit fusion.
p063.s6.b1: Afterward the two returned to the first mansion world to serve with those who welcome the pilgrims of time from Urantia, and they have been assigned to this service indefinitely. They asked to send greetings to Urantia with these revelations, but the request was wisely denied. That mankind’s first parents are still welcoming newly arrived mortals is the warm note on which the paper ends.

p063.s6.b2.q: the most heroic and fascinating chapter in all the history of Urantia

p063.s7.b0: Paper 63 shows that mankind began as one very small family. There was a decision to leave together despite fear, a fire won after repeated failure, a son who led his clan with an injured body, and a teacher who taught the one God again in an age of decline. They did not yet know laughter or altruism, yet within them the noblest traits of humanity were already foreshadowed.

p064.s0.h: Introduction — The Second Half of a Million Years of Human History
p064.s0.b0: Paper 64 tells the story of Urantia’s evolutionary races from the days of Andon and Fonta, through the times of the Planetary Prince, to the end of the ice age. Its author is again a Life Carrier resident on Urantia. He divides the nearly one-million-year history of mankind into two halves: the first roughly matches the days before the Planetary Prince, and the second begins with his arrival and the appearance of the six colored races.
p064.s0.b1: The paper deals with races, but from a Life Carrier’s point of view: its purpose is to record how biological evolution and cultural and spiritual progress rose and fell. The text sets down both the strengths and the limitations of each race, and it states plainly that every race has the same standing before the celestial powers. This commentary follows what the text says, calmly and within those bounds.
p064.s1.h: I. The Andonic Aborigines — Between Mountains, Water, and Ice
p064.s1.b0: Primitive man was hemmed in on every side. To the east rose the high Tibetan plateau; to the south and west lay the expanded Mediterranean, reaching to the Indian Ocean; and to the north the ice was advancing. Even so, the more intelligent groups never turned back to their tree-dwelling cousins in the south. The text suggests that many of man’s earliest religious feelings grew out of this sense of geographic helplessness.

p064.s1.b1.q: mountains to the right, water to the left, and ice in front.

p064.s1.b2: The Andonites avoided the forests, and the cold and hunger of the open lands stimulated action, invention, and resourcefulness. By 950,000 years ago they had spread west as far as France and England and east as far as Java and Tasmania. But as the eastern groups mingled with backward strains, fewer and fewer settlements kept up the worship of the Breath Giver, and this dawn civilization was threatened with extinction.

p064.s1.b3.q: human evolution has made progress only in the open and in the higher latitudes.

p064.s2.h: II–III. The Foxhall Peoples; The Badonan Tribes — Two Embers in an Age of Decline
p064.s2.b0: By 900,000 years ago the arts of Andon and Fonta and the culture of Onagar were vanishing; culture, religion, and even flintworking had reached their lowest ebb. Mixed groups arrived in Europe, and after them the tribes known as the Heidelberg race spread over the continent. Yet through this long decline, two groups at the western and eastern edges kept alive the traditions of Andon.

p064.s3.h: IV. The Neanderthal Races — Half a Million Years Moving with the Glaciers
p064.s3.b0: The Neanderthalers were excellent fighters and hunters. They spread from northwestern India to France, China, and northern Africa, and they dominated the world for almost half a million years. The reindeer supplied them with food, clothing, and tools, and their flintwork improved until it nearly reached the level of Andon’s day. This section is also a record of men and animals moving north and south as the glaciers advanced and retreated.

p064.s3.b2: Yet there was very little progress. For almost a quarter of a million years these peoples lived by hunting and fighting, and the text goes so far as to say that the attempt to produce a new type of intelligent life seemed about to fail. In these spiritually dark ages the Neanderthalers had no religion beyond superstition, and they were deathly afraid of mists, fogs, and the dark. A religion of fear sought to placate unseen forces and in the end led to human sacrifice.

p064.s3.b3.q: And this terrible practice of human sacrifice has been perpetuated by the more backward peoples of Urantia right on down to the twentieth century.

p064.s4.h: V. Origin of the Colored Races — The Nineteen Children of the Sangik Family
p064.s4.b0: Five hundred thousand years ago the Badonan tribes fell into a war that lasted more than a hundred years, and only about one hundred families were left; but these survivors were the most intelligent of all the descendants of Andon and Fonta then living. Then a couple in the northeastern part of the highlands suddenly began to have unusually intelligent children. This was the Sangik family.

p064.s4.b1.q: This was the Sangik family, the ancestors of all of the six colored races of Urantia.

p064.s4.b2: The nineteen Sangik children showed a unique tendency for their skin to turn different colors when exposed to sunlight. These colors grew more pronounced as they matured, and their offspring tended toward the skin color of the Sangik parent.

p064.s4.b5.q: The simultaneous emergence of all six races on Urantia, and in one family, was most unusual.

The share of those who taught without fame was by no means small.

p064.s6.h: VII. Dispersion of the Colored Races — Settling the Continents
p064.s6.b0: While the fifth glacier spread widely, the Sangik peoples lived together around the foothills for almost a hundred thousand years, though a natural antipathy between the different races showed itself early. When the ice retreated, the red man went northeast, closely followed by the yellow man, and the blue man moved northwest into Europe. The orange, green, and indigo races entered Africa one after another over a newly raised land bridge.
p064.s6.b1: In Europe the blue man met the Neanderthalers, descendants of their common ancestor Andon, and mingled with them. The red race left Asia as eleven tribes of a little over seven thousand people, and the small mixed groups accompanying them went south to found the civilizations of Mexico, Central America, and South America. The text adds that any effort to trace the Sangik ancestry of modern peoples must take into account the later admixture of Adamic blood.

p064.s6.b3: The western Andon tribes, pushed by the glaciers to the very edge of the sea, built boats and put out to sea when the last glacier came. They were the first marine adventurers; most perished on the open sea, but some reached Iceland and Greenland, and their Eskimo descendants later crossed to North America. The Life Carrier regrets that so many of the sturdy qualities of these early ancestors have been lost to later races.

p064.s6.b4.q: we miss the magnificent persistency and superb devotion of your early ancestors, which oftentimes bordered on grandeur and sublimity.

p064.s7.b0: Paper 64 is a record in which progress and retrogression endlessly alternate. Superior strains are lost in war, culture sinks to its lowest point, and then it rises again through a single teacher. Through it all the Life Carrier stresses two things: that the tendency to fight among themselves destroyed races and civilizations from within, and that no race stands lower than any other before heaven.

p065.lead: Evolution is never an accident: the inside story of the Urantia life experiment, guided together by the Life Carriers, the physical controllers, and the adjutant mind-spirits.

p065.foot.text: Sponsored by a Life Carrier of Nebadon resident on Urantia

p065.s0.b0: Papers 58 through 64 told, in the order of time, how life appeared and grew on our world. Paper 65 looks at the same history again, this time from the place of those who oversaw it. The author is a Life Carrier resident on Urantia. He explains that basic material life is the work of a threefold creativity: the formulation of the Master Physical Controllers, the life-impartation ministry of the Seven Master Spirits, and the active ministration of the Life Carriers.

p065.s0.b2: The Life Carriers exercise considerable discretionary control over the environment right up to the appearance of human will—the ability to know God and the power of choosing to worship him. Because the integrated work of these three agencies conditions the course of organic evolution, the opening of the paper ends with a clear conclusion.

p065.s0.b3.q: evolution—on Urantia or elsewhere—is always purposeful and never accidental.

p065.s1.h: I. Life Carrier Functions — Three Phases of Being
p065.s1.b0: The Life Carriers possess potentials of personality metamorphosis that few orders of creatures have. They ordinarily work as mid-phase Sons, the state of their origin, but in that state they cannot function in the electrochemical domains where energies and material particles are fashioned into living units. So, as their task requires, commissions of other beings change their phase of existence.

p065.s1.b2: The author himself has worked on Urantia in this third phase ever since the times of Andon and Fonta. The Life Carriers look forward to a possible fourth, wholly spiritual stage when the universe is settled in light and life, but he admits frankly that the technique for reaching it has never been revealed to them. It is striking to hear that even such high beings face a future they do not yet understand.
p065.s2.h: II. The Evolutionary Panorama — From Seaweed to Man
p065.s2.b0: The story of man’s ascent from seaweed to the lordship of earthly creation is a romance of biologic struggle and mind survival. Our primordial ancestors were literally the slime and ooze of the ocean bed in the warm bays and lagoons along the shores of the ancient inland seas. This section retraces that long road by picking out only its key links.

p065.s2.b2: The eastern life group suffered repeated and irretrievable losses of its highest types of germ plasm and so lost its human potential; with the consent of their superiors, the Life Carriers then manipulated the environment to circumscribe those strains. Outwardly it looked accidental, but in reality it was altogether purposeful. The appearance of man during the ice age was likewise planned.

p065.s2.b3.q: this appearance of primitive man on earth during the ice age was not just an accident; it was by design.

p065.s3.h: III. The Fostering of Evolution — Caring Without Interfering
p065.s3.b0: The Life Carriers may use every natural resource and any fortuitous circumstance, but they are not permitted to intervene mechanically in evolution or to manipulate it arbitrarily. This puts the dramatic frog story of Paper 62 in a new light. Had that frog perished, the evolution of mankind would not have ended. The Life Carriers were fostering no fewer than a thousand other strains at the same time, and that frog was their third selection.
p065.s3.b1: Even if Andon and Fonta had been lost before having children, human evolution would only have been delayed, not prevented; afterward no fewer than seven thousand favorable strains could still have developed into a human type. But the human potentials of animal life are now exhausted, and mankind must solve its problems of development with the stocks it already has.

p065.s3.b2.q: In a general way, man’s evolutionary destiny is in his own hands,

p065.s3.b3: Just as the Life Carriers fostered and conserved the life strains before human will appeared, so now man must do this for himself. The author adds that one day his readers may be attached to a corps of Life Carriers and have every opportunity to offer better ideas. “Be patient!” he says.
p065.s4.h: IV. The Urantia Adventure — The Sixtieth Life Experiment
p065.s4.b0: Urantia was assigned as a life-experiment world, the scene of the sixtieth attempt to improve the Satania adaptation of the Nebadon life designs. Here no fewer than twenty-eight features of life modification were worked out. Yet “experiment” does not mean trying things at random. The evolution of life is a progressive and changing technique, but it is never left to chance.

p065.s4.b1.q: The evolution of life is a technique ever progressive, differential, and variable, but never haphazard, uncontrolled, nor wholly experimental, in the accidental sense.

p065.s4.b2: As evidence the author points to the healing of wounds. An injured cell elaborates certain chemicals that stimulate neighboring normal cells; these secrete substances that help healing, and they multiply to replace the cells that were destroyed. This formula was chosen from over one hundred thousand phases and features of possible chemical reactions, and more than half a million experiments were made before it was settled on.

p065.s4.b4: The author foresees that when Urantia scientists learn more about these healing chemicals, they will treat injuries more efficiently and indirectly learn more about controlling certain serious diseases. The Life Carriers later refined the technique on another Satania world, giving more pain relief and better control over the proliferation of the surrounding cells.
p065.s4.b5: Such modification work left behind many apparently useless forms of transition life and countless strange by-products. The author says he can well understand how puzzling these must look from the limited human viewpoint.
p065.s5.h: V. Life-Evolution Vicissitudes — Disappointment and Confidence
p065.s5.b0: The Life Carriers have their regrets. The Caligastia betrayal and the Adamic default handicapped their efforts to modify intelligent life. Their greatest disappointment was the reversion of certain primitive plant life to parasitic bacteria, which caused many distressful diseases in the higher mammals and in man. They had hoped that the admixture of the Adamic life plasm would make the blended race practically immune, but that hope too was dashed.

p065.s5.b1.q: The wise and all-powerful beings who are responsible for universe management undoubtedly know exactly what they are about;

p065.s5.b2: So the fitting attitude, for Life Carriers and mortals alike, is patient waiting and hearty co-operation. There are compensations for tribulation, such as Michael’s bestowal, and the celestial supervisors express complete confidence in the ultimate evolutionary triumph of the human race. This refusal to withdraw trust when plans go astray applies just as well to an individual life.
p065.s6.h: VI. Evolutionary Techniques of Life — An Innate Striving for Perfection
p065.s6.b0: The secret of life cannot be captured by analysis. The chemist can explain the chemistry of dead protoplasm, but because he must kill protoplasm in order to analyze it, he can never grasp the organization and performance of living protoplasm. Yet every living thing carries, along with its power of adaptation, an insatiable craving for ever-increasing perfection.

p065.s6.b1.q: These interminable efforts of all living things evidence the existence within them of an innate striving for perfection.

p065.s6.b3: Physics and chemistry alone, however, cannot explain human evolution. The laws of physics do not respond to training, and chemical reactions are not modified by education, but mind learns from experience. The ability to learn, memory, and differential response to environment are the endowment of mind.

p065.s6.b4.q: Preintelligent organisms react to environmental stimuli, but those organisms which are reactive to mind ministry can adjust and manipulate the environment itself.

p065.s7.h: VII. Evolutionary Mind Levels — The Ministry of the Adjutant Spirits
p065.s7.b0: The seven adjutant spirits are more circuitlike than entitylike. They do not touch purely mechanical responses; they begin to function the moment the ability to learn from experience appears. On Urantia, a life-experiment world, they were relatively isolated, and with but a single exception they had greater difficulty contacting evolving minds here than anywhere else in Nebadon. That is why so many border phenomena appeared, confused mixtures of mechanical and teachable responses.
p065.s7.b1: At the level of the spirit of worship, the higher reaches down to co-ordinate with the lower, and still additional spirit ministry accompanies the work of the spirit of wisdom. All such changes are gradual and reciprocal, never abrupt. The author urges us always to keep three domains distinct.

p065.s8.h: VIII. Evolution in Time and Space — A Choice That Delay Cannot Defeat
p065.s8.b0: Why does evolution take so long? The author answers that life cannot unfold faster than the physical changes of the planet allow. If conditions permitted, the whole evolution of life could be completed in well under a million years, but the Life Carriers have no control over geologic evolution. To short-lived creatures evolution seems endless, but on Paradise, where time is nonexistent, all of it is present.
p065.s8.b1: Just as mind evolution waits on physical conditions, spiritual progress is delayed by limited mental growth. Yet the evolution of the soul does not depend on education or culture. What it needs is the mind’s choice of survival and its decision to do the will of the Father in heaven.

p065.s8.b2.q: Although survival may not depend on the possession of knowledge and wisdom, progression most certainly does.

p065.s8.b3.q: none of these obstacles can defeat the whole-souled choice of will.

p065.s9.b0: Paper 65 presents evolution as a purposeful work of co-operation. Matter is linked to mind and mind to spirit, and the delays and setbacks along the way are not failures but the way things work in time and space. And now that the Life Carriers have withdrawn, mankind’s evolutionary destiny has passed in large measure into our own hands.

p065.s9.b2: Paper 66 turns to Caligastia, the Planetary Prince who arrived almost five hundred thousand years after Andon and Fonta, together with his staff, life at Dalamatia, and the misfortune of Caligastia.
p066.lead: Dalamatia, founded in Mesopotamia half a million years ago: the first world center of culture, led for three hundred thousand years by Caligastia and the one hundred, and the seeds of its tragedy.

p066.foot.text: Presented by a Melchizedek of Nebadon

p066.s0.h: Introduction — A Planetary Prince Who Came Late
p066.s0.b0: Paper 66 is presented by a Melchizedek of Nebadon, and with it the history of Urantia enters an age in which celestial administration meets human society directly. On an average world the advent of the Planetary Prince, a Lanonandek Son, is a sign that will—the ability to choose the path of eternal survival—has developed in the mind of primitive man. On Urantia, however, the Prince arrived almost half a million years after human will appeared.
p066.s0.b1: Caligastia arrived about five hundred thousand years ago, at the time the six Sangik races appeared. Almost one-half billion primitive human beings were scattered over Europe, Asia, and Africa, and the Prince’s headquarters was set up in Mesopotamia, near the center of world population. The paper describes in detail the work done at that headquarters while quietly tracing the weakness of one personality that brought it all down.
p066.s1.h: I. Prince Caligastia — A Brilliant Record and a Hidden Pride
p066.s1.b0: Caligastia was a Lanonandek Son, number 9,344 of the secondary order, experienced in the administration of the local universe. Lucifer elevated him to his personal staff, and he acceptably filled five successive assignments of honor and trust. He sought a commission as Planetary Prince very early, but his request repeatedly failed to win the assent of the Constellation Fathers before he was finally assigned to Urantia.
p066.s1.b1: The author was present on Jerusem when Caligastia departed. No prince of the planets, he recalls, ever set out with a richer preparatory experience or better prospects. He leaves only one hint: a certain characteristic restlessness and a tendency to disagree with the established order in minor matters.

p066.s1.b2.q: I did not then comprehend that Caligastia was insidiously falling in love with himself; I did not then so fully understand the subtleties of personality pride.

p066.s2.h: II. The Prince’s Staff — The Caligastia One Hundred
p066.s2.b0: The Prince did not come alone. At the head of his staff was his associate-assistant Daligastia, and with them came many angelic co-operators and other celestial beings. From our standpoint the most interesting group was the corporeal staff, the Caligastia one hundred. They were chosen from over 785,000 ascendant citizens of Jerusem who volunteered for the Urantia adventure, and each came from a different planet.
p066.s2.b1: Their bodies were prepared in a special way. The Life Carriers chose fifty males and fifty females of the best surviving strains of the Andon and Fonta stock, and a commission from Avalon extracted a portion of their life plasm and transferred it to the material bodies built for the staff. The whole repersonalization took exactly ten days. The text adds that these events gave rise to numerous legends, later confused with the traditions of Adam and Eve.
p066.s3.h: III. Dalamatia — The City of the Prince
p066.s3.b0: The headquarters lay in the Persian Gulf region of those days, in the district later known as Mesopotamia. The one great task of that age was to transform man from a hunter to a herder, and later into a peace-loving, home-abiding farmer. The city was named Dalamatia in honor of Daligastia; it was simple but beautiful, enclosed within a wall forty feet high.
p066.s3.b1: The city was laid out in ten subdivisions, each with the headquarters of one council at its center, and centermost stood the temple of the unseen Father. Buildings were made mostly of brick, and the homes and villages of the surrounding peoples were greatly improved by following this example. The staff continually gathered the superior individuals of nearby tribes, trained them, and sent them back as teachers and leaders of their own peoples.
p066.s4.h: IV. Early Days of the One Hundred — Threefold Beings and the Primary Midwayers
p066.s4.b0: The arrival of the staff made a profound impression, and much later mythology grew out of garbled legends of those days. The serious obstacle was the tendency of mortals to regard them as gods. Yet the one hundred did not resort to supernatural methods or superhuman manipulations. Even so, they were extraordinary beings in three respects.

p066.s4.b2: In the thirty-third year at Dalamatia, number two and number seven of the Danite group accidentally discovered a phenomenon attending the liaison of their morontia selves. The result was the first of the primary midway creatures, and the whole staff, following the same method, brought into being the original corps of 50,000 primary midwayers. Invisible to human beings, these creatures were for ages the sum total of the spirit world to primitive mortals.
p066.s4.b3: The complement of the system circuits was also introduced into the hundred Andonites who had given their germ plasm, so that they lived on with the staff century after century and remained at headquarters as personal attendants. The tree of life grew in the central courtyard of the temple of the unseen Father.

p066.s5.b0: The one hundred were organized into ten autonomous councils of ten members each, and when two or more met together Daligastia presided. A look at the work of each council shows at a glance what the foundations of civilization are made of.

p066.s5.b2.q: Urantia civilization was literally forged out between the anvil of necessity and the hammers of fear.

p066.s5.b3: Hap’s group held to the principle that revelation must not complicate evolution, but it yielded to the city dwellers’ desire for a form of worship and gave them seven chants and “⟦Q 66:5.14⟧the Father’s prayer⟦/Q⟧.” The prayer asks for deliverance from fear, truth on our lips, respect for what belongs to our neighbors, and the wish to do the Father’s will on this world as others do on worlds beyond.

p066.s5.b4.q: Deliver us from the fear of all save you.

p066.s5.b5: Sadly, the alphabet and many other achievements were lost in the confusion of rebellion, and much was not rediscovered until the twentieth century. The Caligastia defection also destroyed the hope of a universal language for untold ages.
p066.s6.h: VI. The Prince’s Reign — Evolution, Not Revolution
p066.s6.b0: When the one hundred arrived, the whole world was caught in the stalemate of tradition-bound mores. Tradition gives stability and co-operation but stifles initiative and enslaves creative powers. The one hundred proclaimed a new gospel of individual initiative, yet they did not try to transform the primitive races suddenly. Though they knew the arts and culture of Jerusem, they did not simply transplant them.

p066.s6.b2.q: Their motive was progression by evolution and not revolution by revelation.

p066.s6.b3: The text warns that overteaching and overenlightenment bring confusion and dismay and can rob people of the little progress they have gained over long ages. When we help others, pace and respect matter just as much as good intentions.
p066.s7.h: VII. Life in Dalamatia — Home, School, and the Father’s Way
p066.s7.b0: The city was beautiful but modest, and the land within its walls could provide pasture and gardens for about twenty thousand people. No methods were used at this headquarters that did not naturally belong on Urantia. The staff had no children of their own, but their fifty pattern homes sheltered no fewer than five hundred adopted children, who after the Prince’s schools were sent as emissaries to the tribes of their own races.
p066.s7.b1: The order of settled family life also dates from this time. The home never succeeded as a social unit until people learned to love and plan for their grandchildren and their grandchildren’s children. The school Fad sponsored was an industrial school where pupils learned by doing, valuing both individual training and socialization in groups.

p066.s7.b2.q: Savage man loves his child, but civilized man loves also his grandchild.

head: The Father’s Way — the seven commands given by Hap
rows: You shall not fear nor serve any God but the Father of all.
You shall not disobey the Father’s Son, the world’s ruler, nor show disrespect to his superhuman associates.
You shall not speak a lie when called before the judges of the people.
You shall not kill men, women, or children.
You shall not steal your neighbor’s goods or cattle.
You shall not touch your friend’s wife.
You shall not show disrespect to your parents or to the elders of the tribe.

p066.s7.b4: This was the law of Dalamatia for almost three hundred thousand years, and people held one command in mind for each day of the week, using it in greetings and mealtime thanksgiving. The seven-day week itself was introduced by the Dalamatia teachers as one fourth of the twenty-eight-day lunar month. The text also states plainly that farming is not a penalty for sin.

p066.s7.b5.q: Work with the soil is not a curse; rather is it the highest blessing to all who are thus permitted to enjoy the most human of all human activities.

p066.s8.h: VIII. Misfortunes of Caligastia — Pride That Ended in Betrayal
p066.s8.b0: Looking over Caligastia’s long career, the author finds only one outstanding feature: he was ultraindividualistic and mildly resented all forms of supervision. Yet whenever a test came he proved loyal, so no real fault was found in him before his betrayal. Both Lucifer and Caligastia were patiently instructed and lovingly warned about their critical tendencies and pride, but they misconstrued this help as unwarranted criticism and interference with their liberty.

p066.s8.b1.q: They judged their unselfish advisers by their own evolving selfishness.

p066.s8.b2: For almost three hundred thousand years after the Prince arrived, planetary civilization progressed in a fairly normal manner, but at the Lucifer rebellion Caligastia went into darkness. He was deprived of sovereign authority, his power was greatly curtailed by the incarnation of Machiventa Melchizedek, and in the days of Michael he was finally shorn of all authority. He now awaits the final adjudication of the Ancients of Days.
p066.s8.b3: What the paper stresses last is the dignity of human free will. The teaching that a personal devil can overpower the normal human mind against its own choosing is, the text says, wholly fictitious. Even the indwelling Adjuster refuses to compel a single thought or act against man’s own will.

p066.s8.b4.q: The free will of man is supreme in moral affairs;

p066.s9.b0: Paper 66 shows how concrete the foundations of civilization are: wells and food storage, domestic animals and the wheel, letters and schools, hygiene and law, and homes where grandparents love their grandchildren. It also shows that all of this can be undone by the hidden pride of a single leader. Yet nothing can replace or take away the moral choices human beings make for themselves.
